source.title: Open problems for tractability of multivariate integration

accepted.question_text: For integration of real functions on [0,1]^d whose mixed partial derivatives up to order r(d) are uniformly bounded, if d/r(d) stays bounded as d grows, is the number of function values needed for relative error epsilon not bounded by any polynomial in d and epsilon^{-1}?

For integration of infinitely differentiable real functions on [0,1]^d whose partial derivatives are all bounded by one, is the number of function values needed for relative error epsilon not bounded by any polynomial in d and epsilon^{-1}?

For integration in the weighted Sobolev Hilbert space on [0,1]^d with kernel product_{j=1}^d (1 + gamma_j min(x_j,t_j)), positive nonincreasing weights gamma_j, and sum gamma_j finite, if s_gamma = inf {s>0 : sum gamma_j^s is finite}, is the strong-tractability exponent p* equal to max(1, 2 s_gamma)?

For integration in the weighted Sobolev Hilbert space on [0,1]^d with kernel product_{j=1}^d (1 + gamma_j min(x_j,t_j)) and summable positive nonincreasing weights gamma_j, is the strong-tractability exponent p* equal to 1 if and only if sum gamma_j^{1/2} is finite?

For randomized integration in the weighted Sobolev Hilbert space on [0,1]^d with kernel product_{j=1}^d (1 + gamma_j min(x_j,t_j)) and positive nonincreasing weights gamma_j, is sum gamma_j^2 finite a necessary condition for strong tractability?

For randomized integration in the weighted Sobolev Hilbert space on [0,1]^d with kernel product_{j=1}^d (1 + gamma_j min(x_j,t_j)) and positive nonincreasing weights gamma_j, is limsup_{d->infinity} (sum_{j=1}^d gamma_j^2)/ln d finite a necessary condition for tractability?

trace.notes: Normalized the input as one zbMATH resolver URL with identifier 1967220.

Direct zbMATH browser access did not expose the record and local shell fetches hit Cloudflare/DNS failures. Local resolver metadata identified the exact title and DOI; exact-title/DOI search recovered the ScienceDirect open-archive article with matching title and DOI, and its visible article body was used as the primary HTML source.

Mapped ScienceDirect HTML article: article metadata and abstract; Section 1 Introduction; Section 2 worst-case tractability definitions; Section 3 smooth functions with Open Problem 1; Section 4 weighted Sobolev spaces with Open Problem 2; Section 5 randomized setting with Open Problem 3; acknowledgements and references.
Sections 1 and 2 define tractability, strong tractability, n(epsilon,F_d), and the worst-case setting; no standalone open-problem block appears there.

Extracted Open Problem 2 with two explicit subquestions about the exponent of strong tractability for weighted Sobolev spaces.
Extracted Open Problem 3 with two explicit subquestions about necessary conditions for randomized strong tractability and tractability.
Expanded F_{d,r(d)}, the integration functional, information complexity, and intractability using Sections 2 and 3.
Expanded F_{d,infinity} as infinitely differentiable functions with all partial derivatives bounded by one, and stated intractability in terms of polynomial dependence on d and epsilon^{-1}.
Expanded the weighted Sobolev RKHS, weights, sum condition, sum-exponent, and strong-tractability exponent.
Expanded the weaker exponent-one version of Open Problem 2 with the weighted Sobolev setting and gamma_j^{1/2} summability condition.
Expanded randomized algorithms and the Monte Carlo strong-polynomial condition before asking whether that condition is necessary for randomized strong tractability.
Expanded the randomized weighted Sobolev setting and the limsup gamma_j^2/log d condition for tractability.
